text:
alex: heads up — we started seeing inference p99 jump in eastus2 around 02:12 UTC. graphs show steady p99 ~120ms -> spikes to ~380ms and many tcp retransmits. anyone touching host QoS or network shaping?

infra-bot: alert: telemetry/inference/p99-eastus2 breached threshold at 2025-11-09T02:15:03Z. linked traces: https://telemetry.internal/r/tx/abcd1234

sara: I didn't touch anything intentionally. I can ssh into a few implicated hosts and run quick checks. which hosts are highest error rate?

alex: logs point to gpu-node-57, gpu-node-58, and ~10 others in the same AZ. traces show higher gRPC latencies on east-west calls (pod->pod on same host and cross-host). packet retransmits visible on tcp level.

eli: quick hypothesis: host-level shaping (tbf/police) applied to an interface accidentally during a change to limit noisy tenants. If egress is artificially limited it can cause microbursts to be dropped and increase tail latency for small RPCs.

ops-oncall: running basic checks now. pulling tc state from one of the nodes:

```
# tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc tbf 1: root refcnt 2 rate 80Mbit burst 10Kb lat 50ms
 Sent 1234567 bytes 1234 pkt (dropped 452, overlimits 452 requeues 0)
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
qdisc fq_codel 2:1 parent 1:fff1 limit 1000p flows 1024 quantum 300 target 5.0ms interval 100.0ms
 Sent 987654 bytes 987 pkt (dropped 12, overlimits 3 requeues 1)
```

ops-oncall: whoa — TBF at 80Mbit on eth0 and fq_codel on top. drops showing on tbf counters.

sara: that matches RU traces — we saw bursts from KV-cache syncs and small RPCs that need low latency. TBF burst size is only 10Kb so it will clip short bursts and cause tail retransmits. Where did that tbf come from?

alex: change was part of "noisy-tenant rate limit" rollout earlier this week. config was intended for trunk veths used by a subset of tenants, but looks like a script applied it to host eth0 on some GPU nodes.

eli: also check if egress was applied to the wrong qdisc hierarchy. tbf on root can be very disruptive. need to confirm CNI/device mapping — calico's iptables/ebpf hooks can interact with tc.

sara: I'm going to remove the tbf on one node as a canary and measure. command: 

```
# tc qdisc del dev eth0 root
# tc qdisc add dev eth0 root fq_codel limit 10000
```

ops-oncall: canary run on gpu-node-57: removed tbf, added fq_codel. immediate p99 dropped back toward baseline within 20s. tcp retransmits stopped in that host's traces.

alex: good. what's the blast radius? how many hosts have the bad tbf?

ops-oncall: scanning fleet via salt: found ~78 hosts with an unintended root tbf (mostly in eastus2 AZ and one on-prem rack).

eli: runbook note: tbf was added by automation job id job-4523, which had a grep bug that matched eth* and applied to physical NICs as well as veths.

sara: temporary mitigation: roll back job-4523 and remove tbf from all affected hosts. I'm kicking a job to remove tbf and replace with fq_codel where appropriate. doing this in batches of 10, monitoring p99 and packet drop counters after each batch.

alex: can we also patch the automation so it targets container veths only (prefix veth*) and not host NICs?

eli: yes — PR incoming. Also recommend adding an invariant check in CI that refuses to apply root qdisc changes to interfaces with label "gpu-host".

ops-oncall: note — some hosts still show offload flags that interact with fq_codel. we saw GSO/GRO causing reordering/large segments — if we flip qdiscs we should verify ethtool offloads. command to check: `ethtool -k eth0`

sara: on the remediation run I'll also set `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` temporarily for a subset to ensure correct small-packet behavior for RPCs, then revert if not needed.

alex: long-term: avoid hard rate limits at host root qdisc. prefer CNI-level shaping per-tenant, or use policing on veths with proper classful qdisc and large bursts for short RPCs. Also add a canary in telemetry to detect sudden per-host tc drop counters > 0.

eli: one more gotcha — RDMA-enabled nodes fall back to IP path if the RDMA route is overloaded; the fallback path hits host qdiscs. luckily RDMA mostly unaffected but once IP fallback gets hit, tails blow up. add alert for RDMA fallbacks.

ops-oncall: rolling rollback in progress — batch 1 done (10 hosts). p99 across cluster down 60ms after batch 1. continuing.

sara: filed INC-2025-178 with timeline and cluster list. assigning follow-ups: patch automation (eli), fleet sweep to verify qdisc state (ops-oncall), add telemetry alert (alex), patch runbook + CI check (sara).

alex: thanks all. once rollback completes let's have a postmortem with root cause and detection improvements. :thumbsup:
